mainTopic: How רבי and רבנן disagree about a lost חטאת and its replacement: splitting the משנה, and the two versions of רב (רב הונא and רבי אבא)
overview: The גמרא is working out whether the two clauses of the משנה about a lost חטאת and its replacement can follow one opinion. First it suggests that both fit רבנן, because if the owner simply took one and offered it, everyone agrees the other dies. According to רבי אבא in the name of רב, that answer does not work, so the רישא must follow רבנן and the סיפא must follow רבי. The גמרא asks what this adds when the dispute is stated openly later. It answers that the open dispute teaches that the point where the unnamed clauses clash is a real מחלוקת. Then the גמרא looks at רב הונא's version of רב, where the argument depends on whether the חכמים made a תקנה for קדשים. רב משרשיא challenges this from a ברייתא about eating holy food, and the גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבנן only. Finally, the גמרא brings רבי אבא's version and challenges it from the משנה about the extra goat of יום כיפור, together with רב's own comment on it. The answer to that challenge comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Both clauses can fit the Rabbis if the owner just took one and offered it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the סיפא can also follow רבנן. Even רבנן agree that if the owner took one and offered it, the other one is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees that if a person took one and sacrificed it, the second one is left to die. So you can explain the last clause as a case where he took one of them and sacrificed it, and then it is everyone's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the last clause of the משנה can match רבנן too. It explains that clause as a case where the owner went ahead, took one, and offered it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally רבנן do not send the extra animal or money to die. But here the owner acted on his own and offered one without asking, so even רבנן agree the other one is left to die. Because of this, the סיפא no longer needs to follow only רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees (even the side that usually argues)
Took / pulled (here: took one animal or sum on his own)
Is left to die (a חטאת that cannot be used is locked up until it dies)
You can find it, meaning you can explain the case this way
The opinion of everyone

phrases.english: All agree
that if he took one and sacrificed it
that the second one is left to die,
you can find it (explain the last clause)
such as where he took one of them and sacrificed,
and it is the opinion of all.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים שֶׁאִם מָשַׁךְ אַחַת וְהִקְרִיבָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (before this section) about whether the clauses of the משנה can all follow רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the סיפא so that it fits both opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא, which sends the extra one to die, seemed to follow only רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא is a case where the owner took one and offered it, and there everyone agrees, so both clauses fit רבנן.

steps.title: According to רבי אבא citing רב, that answer does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי אבא in the name of רב, who explains the dispute differently. His version blocks the answer just given.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי אבא in the name of רב, who said: Everyone agrees that if a person gets atonement with the one that was not lost, the lost one is left to die. What do they argue about? When he gets atonement with the lost one. רבי holds that an animal set aside in place of a lost one is treated like the lost one. רבנן hold it is not treated like the lost one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the last answer does not work according to רבי אבא's explanation of the dispute. It quotes that explanation in full to set up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אבא, the argument is not about whether the owner took one on his own. It is about which animal was offered. If the replacement was offered, everyone agrees the lost one dies. If the original lost one was offered, רבי says the replacement dies like a lost animal, and רבנן say it does not. So the case of 'he took one and offered it' does not automatically make everyone agree.

keyTerms.meaning: Gets atonement (through offering a particular animal)
The lost one (the original animal that was lost and later found)
They disagreed
One set aside in place of a lost animal (the replacement)
Is treated like the lost one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two animals. 'אבודה' is the ORIGINAL animal that got lost. 'מפריש לאיבוד' is the REPLACEMENT set aside because of the loss.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Abba citing Rav,
who said:
All agree when one gets atonement with the one that was not lost
that the lost one is left to die.
About what do they disagree?
When one gets atonement with the lost one,
for Rebbi holds:
one set aside in place of a lost one is like the lost one,
phrases.notes: So the replacement dies, just as a lost one would if the other had been offered.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold:
it is not like the lost one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 1 fails according to רבי אבא's version of the dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that both clauses of the משנה follow רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי אבא, רבנן do not send the replacement to die even when one animal was offered. So 'he took one and offered it' cannot make the סיפא everyone's opinion.

steps.title: The first clause follows the Rabbis and the last clause follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אבא, the משנה must be split. The רישא is a סתם following רבנן, and the סיפא is a סתם following רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause was taught to us without a name, following רבנן. The last clause was taught to us without a name, following רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that, according to רבי אבא, the two clauses of the משנה follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the סיפא cannot be explained as everyone's opinion, it must follow רבי. The רישא still follows רבנן. So the תנא taught each clause as a סתם, with no name, but each one follows a different side.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause
The last clause
Taught without a name, as if it were the plain halacha

phrases.english: The first clause he taught us unattributed, like the Rabbis,
the last clause he taught us unattributed, like Rebbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא סְתַם לַן כְּרַבָּנַן, סֵיפָא סְתַם לַן כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the forced answer according to רבי אבא's view from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the משנה between two opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses of the משנה follow one opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי אבא, the רישא follows רבנן and the סיפא follows רבי.

steps.title: Why hint at the dispute when it is taught openly later?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the split answer. If the point is to show that רבי and רבנן argue, that argument is already stated openly in a later clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the תנא teaching us, that רבי and רבנן disagree? He already teaches the dispute of רבי and רבנן openly in the last clause: If a person set aside a חטאת and it got lost, and he set aside another in its place, and afterward the first one was found, and both are standing, one is offered and the other is left to die. These are the words of רבי. The חכמים say: a חטאת is left to die only if it was found after the owner got atonement, and money goes to the ים המלח only if it was found after the owner got atonement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the תנא split the משנה between two opinions. It quotes the later clause where the dispute is stated openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching two unnamed clauses that follow different opinions would only tell us that there is a dispute. But the משנה already says outright that רבי and חכמים argue. So the split seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asking what new point is being made)
Openly, explicitly
The owner got atonement (his חטאת was already offered)
The Dead Sea, where forbidden money is thrown so no one can use it

steps.whyThisMatters: Normally a משנה does not teach the same point twice. So the גמרא will need to find a different purpose for the unnamed clauses, or a different explanation of them.

phrases.english: And what is he teaching us,
that Rebbi and the Rabbis disagree?
He teaches it explicitly:
the dispute of Rebbi and the Rabbis in the latter clause:
One who designates a sin offering and it was lost,
and he designated another in its place,
and afterward the first was found,
and both of them are standing (fit to be offered)
one of them is offered,
and the second is left to die,
the words of Rebbi.
And the Sages say:
a sin offering is not left to die
unless it was found after the owner got atonement,
and money does not go to the Dead Sea
unless it was found after the owner got atonement!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דִּפְלִיגִי רַבִּי וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the split answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רישא follows רבנן and the סיפא follows רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Splitting the clauses would only show that רבי and רבנן disagree, but the משנה already states their dispute openly. So the split would teach nothing new.

steps.title: The later clause shows there is a dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the סיפא is needed to teach that this law is a מחלוקת between רבי and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה is teaching us: this matter is a dispute between רבי and רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4. It explains what the openly stated dispute in the later clause adds: it tells us that the two unnamed clauses, which seem to contradict each other, really reflect a dispute between רבי and רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 asked why the משנה would split its unnamed rulings between רבי and רבנן if their dispute is stated openly later anyway. The answer is that the openly stated dispute is what teaches us something: the point on which the two unnamed clauses seemed to contradict each other is exactly where רבי and רבנן disagree. So the unnamed clauses are not a contradiction. Each one follows a different side.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
A dispute between opinions

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
this matter is a dispute between Rabbi and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: "This matter" means the law that looked like it was said one way in the רישא and another way in the סיפא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4 and closes the discussion of the split משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the wording is needed: the split teaches that a dispute exists here.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The split anonymous rulings look pointless, because the dispute is stated openly later.
steps.terutzMaskana: The openly stated dispute in the later clause teaches that the matter on which the unnamed clauses differ is a מחלוקת between רבי and רבנן.

steps.title: רב's explanation of where רבי and רבנן disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of רב: everyone agrees that if the owner just offered one, the other dies. They argue only when he comes to ask. רבי holds there is no תקנה for קדשים, and רבנן hold there is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Going back to the statement itself: רב הונא said in the name of רב: Everyone agrees that if the owner took one animal and offered it, the second one is left to die. They argue only when he comes to ask. רבי holds the חכמים did not make a protective enactment for holy things, so we tell him: get atonement with the one that was not lost, and the lost one dies. רבנן hold they did make such an enactment, so we tell him: get atonement with the lost one, and the one that was not lost goes out to graze.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to look at רב הונא's statement in the name of רב on its own. It lays out exactly where רבי and רבנן disagree and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no argument when the owner has already acted and offered one animal; the other dies either way. The argument is about what the בית דין tells him to do before he acts. It all depends on whether the חכמים made a תקנה for קדשים: רבי says no, so the lost animal dies, and רבנן say yes, so the found animal is offered and the other one grazes.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: returning to a statement quoted earlier, to look at it on its own
Everyone agrees
Comes to ask (the בית דין) what to do
A protective enactment made by the חכמים
The animal that was lost
It shall graze (it is put out to pasture, not left to die)

steps.whatToRemember: No one argues after the fact: if he already offered one, the other dies. The dispute is only about what we tell him beforehand. It depends on whether there is a תקנה for קדשים (רבי: no; רבנן: yes).
steps.confusionAlert: Under רבי the lost animal dies, and under רבנן the lost animal is the one offered. Do not mix up which animal each side sends to be offered.

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself:
Rav Huna said that Rav said:
All agree that if he took one
and offered it, the second one is left to die.
They disagree only when he comes to ask.
For Rabbi holds:
they did not make a protective enactment for holy things,
so we tell you: get atonement with the one that was not lost,
and the lost one dies.
And the Rabbis hold:
they did make a protective enactment for holy things,
so we tell you: get atonement with the lost one,
and the one that was not lost shall graze.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The discussion of the משנה is finished, so the גמרא goes back to look closely at רב הונא's statement, which was quoted earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that after the fact the second animal dies. When the owner comes to ask, רבי (no תקנה for קדשים) tells him to offer the one that was not lost, the replacement, and the lost one dies. רבנן (there is a תקנה) tell him to offer the lost one that was found, and the one that was not lost grazes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next challenge: is it really possible that someone holds the חכמים made no תקנה for קדשים?

steps.title: Challenge: the חכמים did make arrangements for holy food
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא asks how anyone could say there is no תקנה for קדשים, since a ברייתא teaches that כהנים add ordinary food or תרומה when the holy portion is small, so that it is eaten with a full stomach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא objected: Did the חכמים really not make an enactment for holy things? But a ברייתא teaches: Why does the פסוק say "they shall eat"? It teaches that if the amount to eat was small, they eat ordinary food and תרומה along with it, so that it is eaten while full.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא challenges the idea, which רב gave to רבי in Step 6, that the חכמים made no protective enactment for קדשים. He brings a ברייתא that seems to show such care.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6, רבי's view depended on 'no תקנה for קדשים'. The ברייתא shows that the eating of holy food was regulated so that it would be eaten properly, with a full meal. So it seems there clearly are arrangements made for the sake of קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
Ordinary, non-holy food
The portion of produce given to a כהן
While full, as part of a satisfying meal

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya objected:
And did they not make an enactment for holy things?
But it was taught in a baraita:
"They shall eat" — why does the verse say it?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:9, about the כהנים eating what is left of the מנחה.

phrases.english: It teaches that if the amount to eat was small,
they eat ordinary food and terumah along with it,
so that it will be eaten while full.
phrases.notes: So the holy food is part of a filling meal, not just a tiny bite on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹתֵיב רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: וְלֹא עָשׂוּ תַּקָּנָה בַּקֳּדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle 'לא עשו תקנה בקדשים' that Step 6 gave as רבי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 6 that, according to רבי, the חכמים made no תקנה for קדשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that care and arrangements were made for how holy food is eaten, so it seems the חכמים do make arrangements for קדשים.

steps.title: Second half of the ברייתא: no extra food when there is a lot
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: when there is a large amount of holy food, the כהנים do not eat ordinary food or תרומה with it, so it will not be eaten while overstuffed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the פסוק say "they shall eat it"? It teaches that if the amount to eat was large, they do not eat ordinary food and תרומה with it, so that it will not be eaten while overstuffed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא that רב משרשיא is using for his challenge. This half covers the opposite case, when there is a lot to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Together, the two halves show careful rules for both a small amount and a large amount of holy food. When there is a lot, no other food is added, so that the holy food is all eaten and none is left over and wasted. That is a protective arrangement for קדשים, which is exactly what רב משרשיא needs. Step 9 finishes his challenge, and Step 10 answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: A large amount
Overstuffed, eating past the point of being full

phrases.english: "They shall eat it" — why does the verse say it?
phrases.notes: The same פסוק, ויקרא 6:9, which says "eat" a second time.

phrases.english: That if the amount to eat was large,
they do not eat ordinary food and terumah with it,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא נֶאֱכֶלֶת עַל הַגַּסָּה.
phrases.english: so that it will not be eaten while overstuffed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that Step 7 started quoting as the basis for the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים do make arrangements (תקנות) for קדשים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on ויקרא 6:9, which explains both 'יאכלו' and 'יאכלוה' as rules about how holy food is eaten.

steps.title: Isn't the ברייתא even according to רבי?
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא finishes his challenge: the ברייתא about making a rule to protect holy food should hold even for רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that this ברייתא holds even according to רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא is finishing the challenge he started in Step 7. He asks whether the ברייתא, which shows that the חכמים made rules to protect holy food, must also be the view of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said that רבי holds there is no תקנה for קדשים. If even רבי agrees with the ברייתא, then he does believe in making rules for holy things. That would contradict רב הונא's version of רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: "Isn't it that...?" A way of pushing for a certain reading of a source

phrases.english: What, is it not even according to Rabbi?
phrases.notes: "It" means the ברייתא from Steps 7 and 8 about adding other food so the holy food is eaten properly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge built in Steps 7 and 8 by aiming the ברייתא at רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that רבי holds there is no תקנה for קדשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא is unattributed and holds even for רבי, then רבי accepts making rules for holy things.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows only the רבנן, not רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is the view of the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב משרשיא very briefly. The ברייתא is only the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן already hold there is a תקנה for קדשים, so the ברייתא fits them well. רבי can still hold there is no such תקנה, so רב הונא's version stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי here

phrases.english: No, it is the Rabbis.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to one side of the מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is everyone's view, including רבי's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only the רבנן's view, so רבי can still hold there is no תקנה for קדשים.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's version survives: the ברייתא about protecting holy food is only the view of the רבנן.

steps.title: רבי אבא's different version of רב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes רב differently. Everyone agrees that if he atones with the animal that was not lost, the lost one dies. They argue when he atones with the lost one, over whether a replacement counts like a lost animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב: everyone agrees that if a person gains atonement with the animal that was not lost, the lost one is left to die. What do they argue about? A case where he gains atonement with the lost one. רבי holds that an animal set aside in place of a lost one counts like a lost animal, so it dies. The רבנן hold it does not count like a lost animal, so it only grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different version of what רב said about the argument between רבי and רבנן. This version changes which case is agreed on and which case is argued about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הונא's version, the argument was about whether there is a תקנה for קדשים. Here the argument is about a different question: does the replacement animal get the status of a lost animal? רבי says yes, so it dies. The רבנן say no, so it grazes until it gets a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
The owner gains atonement by offering the animal
The animal that was lost
Setting aside an animal to replace one that was lost
It is treated like a lost animal

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two animals. The "lost" animal is the original one that went missing and was later found. The replacement is the new one set aside after it was lost.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba says that Rav says:
All agree that when one gains atonement
with the one that was not lost, the lost one dies.
About what do they disagree?
Where one gains atonement with the lost one,
for Rabbi holds: one set aside for a lost animal
is considered like the lost one,
phrases.notes: So for רבי, the leftover replacement is treated like the lost animal and is left to die.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold: it is not considered like the lost one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of רב's statement, next to רב הונא's version from Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that if he atones with the animal that was not lost, the lost one dies. If he atones with the lost one, רבי says the replacement dies, and the רבנן say it grazes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a new version of the argument, and the next steps will test it.

steps.title: The משנה about the extra goat of יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in יומא: the extra goat grazes and is sold, because a communal חטאת does not die. This implies that an individual's חטאת would die.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: the second goat grazes until it gets a blemish, then it is sold, and its money goes to gift offerings, because a communal חטאת is not left to die. This implies that an individual's חטאת is left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a challenge to רבי אבא's version. It quotes a משנה about the goats of יום כיפור and draws an inference from it. The full challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a reason: the goat does not die because it belongs to the community. That reason implies that if it belonged to one person, it would die. The גמרא will use this inference against רבי אבא's version.

keyTerms.meaning: It grazes until it gets a blemish
Gift offerings bought with leftover money
A חטאת brought for the whole community
A single person, as opposed to the community

phrases.english: We learned: The second shall graze until it becomes blemished,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in יומא. The first pair's שעיר לעזאזל died, so a new pair was brought, and now there is an extra goat.

phrases.english: and be sold, and its money will go to gift offerings,
for a communal sin offering does not die.
This implies that an individual's does die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to the version of רב given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a source showing that an individual's leftover חטאת dies. The next step pins down exactly which case this is.

steps.title: רב's own comment makes the challenge sharp
steps.stepSummary: רב said that living animals are not pushed off, so he can atone with the goat from the first pair. The goat of the second pair is like a replacement for a lost animal, and still an individual's would die.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: living animals are not pushed off. So when he gains atonement, he may use the second goat of the first pair, and the other goat, from the later pair, is like one set aside in place of a lost animal. The only reason it does not die is that it belongs to the community. This implies that an individual's would die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge using רב's own words about this משנה. רב explains that the goat of the later pair is like a replacement animal, and the משנה implies that an individual's replacement would die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the atonement is with the original goat of the first pair, and the leftover is the replacement. The משנה implies that an individual's replacement would die, with no argument mentioned. But in רבי אבא's version of רב, the רבנן say a replacement does not count like a lost animal, so it should only graze. This is the problem. The answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Living animals are not permanently pushed off. The goat stays fit even after its partner died
A pair. Here, the pair of goats of יום כיפור
The later one. Here, the goat from the second pair

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the goat of the first pair was not actually lost, the goat of the second pair counts as a "replacement." It was set aside only because something happened to the first pair.
